haiku-low.q1: It gets a 401 at the edge after the key lookup fails. It never reaches the RL store, so no rate-limit counter is affected.
haiku-low.q2: One budget per customer is shared across all their keys, so the total is the customer's per-minute limit: 100 on Standard. Enterprise is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q3: A 429 with a Retry-After header. The backend service is never called for that request.
haiku-low.q4: No. Rejected requests do not increment the counter, so 429s are free.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The increment happens before proxying, so the slot is used. This is intended.
haiku-low.q6: The request is proxied to svc anyway, ratelimit_store_unavailable is bumped once, there is no retry, the call is not counted, and no X-RateLimit headers are returned.
haiku-low.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is an open question with no number. Product has not decided.
haiku-low.q8: Redis holds per-customer keys rl:{customerId}:{minute}, shared by all six edges. Old keys are removed only by their 120s TTL.
haiku-low.q9: Each new UTC minute uses a new key, so the count starts again at zero. Old keys expire through their TTL.
haiku-low.q10: Redis runs one script at a time and the script is atomic, so two edges cannot both take the last slot.
haiku-low.q11: It is the seconds left in the current UTC minute, rounded up, with a minimum of 1.
haiku-low.q12: No retry happens. The client gets the svc response with no X-RateLimit headers, because remaining is unknown.

sonnet.q1: It gets a 401 (unknown/bad/missing key). It never hits the RL store, so no counter is affected.
sonnet.q2: One shared budget per customer across all their keys (key is rl:{customerId}:{minute}), so the plan limit in total (e.g. 100/min on Standard).
sonnet.q3: A 429 with Retry-After (seconds left in the minute). The backend svc is not called.
sonnet.q4: No. 429s do not increment the counter, so they are free.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The incr already happened before proxying, so a backend 500 still costs a slot (intended).
sonnet.q6: The proxy lets the call through to svc anyway, bumps the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric, and the call isn't counted. The response has no RL headers.
sonnet.q7: Standard: 100/min. Enterprise: NOT STATED (open question, Product hasn't decided).
sonnet.q8: In the Redis RL store, in key rl:{customerId}:{minute}, shared by all 6 edges. Old keys are removed by Redis via the TTL (120s set on create); nothing else removes them.
sonnet.q9: At the next UTC minute boundary: fixed windows, each new minute is a new key so the count starts at 0. Minute is taken from Redis TIME.
sonnet.q10: The check-and-INCR runs as an atomic Lua script in Redis, and Redis runs one script at a time, so two edges can't both take the last slot.
sonnet.q11: Seconds left in the current minute (based on Redis TIME), rounded up, minimum 1.
sonnet.q12: No retry (one shot). The client gets the svc response with no X-RateLimit-* headers, since remaining isn't known.
